title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the continuation of 'La Longue Marche', in the computations around the 'Teichmüller' group G_3 (presented by generators ρ and σ, with the usual PSL2/SL2-type relations). G_3 is extended by a module M with basis λ_0, λ_1 (with δ = λ_1 − λ_0), giving G_{ρ,σ}. The group is then divided by the subgroup μ_G and further extended by a group of 'units' O_12^*. These units act through automorphisms u_μ defined in (150, 151): u_μ(ζ) = ζ^μ and u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ, where ν = ν(μ) = (μ−1)/2.

On the previous page Grothendieck fixed a splitting (ρ' = ξρ, σ' = ησ) of the extension, with ξ = a_0λ_0 + a_1λ_1 and η = bδ. The scalars a_0, a_1, b are subject to a linear relation (later written −2a_0 + 2a_1 − 3b + 1 = 0). His aim is to classify the lifts O_12^* → G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G that are compatible with this splitting, i.e. that commute with ρ' and σ'.

Step 1. Let H(ρ',σ') (258) be the centralizer of the pair (ρ',σ') in G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G. Its image in (G_3)_{ρ_0} ≅ (G_{ρ,σ}/M)/O_12^* commutes with the images of ρ and σ. Since ρ and σ generate, that image lies in the centre of (G_3)_{ρ_0}, and the centre is trivial. Hence H(ρ',σ') ⊂ O_12^*·M, whose elements are written λu_μ with λ ∈ ΓM and μ ∈ ΓO_12^* (259).

Step 2. Compute the condition for λu_μ to fix ρ'. We have (λu_μ)(ρ') = int(λ)(ζ^μ λ_1^ν ρ) = λζ^μλ_1^ν ρ(λ^{-1}) ρ. Setting this equal to ζρ, and writing M additively, gives λ + μζ + νλ_1 − ρ(λ) = ζ. Using μ − 1 = 2ν, this becomes (1−ρ)λ + 2νζ + νλ_1 = 0, which is the first equation of the next page.

On the next page the same is done for σ', giving (1−σ)λ + 2νη = 0. Writing λ = xλ_0 + yλ_1 turns everything into a small linear system for x and y, proportional to ν. The upshot is that the centralizer is essentially a graph over O_12^*, so compatible lifts exist and are unique up to the expected ambiguity. This is a concrete, low-level step in determining the automorphisms and splittings of profinite or pro-unipotent extensions of the genus-0 / modular Teichmüller group by a Tate-twist-like module.
errors: Notation drift: ζ is used here for the element called ξ on the previous page (ξ = a_0λ_0 + a_1λ_1); the next page reverts to ξ.
Equation numbering is inconsistent: (258) and (259) are reused on the next page, and the next page refers to (261) and (257) in ways that do not match the labels written.

The step 'image in the centre, hence trivial' relies on the centre of (G_3)_{ρ_0} being trivial. This is asserted, not proved, on this page; presumably it was established earlier. Fine for the PSL2(Z)-type group generated by ρ and σ of orders 3 and 2.

Minor: the additive translation silently identifies the conjugation int(λ) with λ·(−)·ρ(λ^{-1}), i.e. it uses M abelian and normal. This is correct, but it merges the multiplicative group and the additive module notation.

ideas.what: Centralizer of a splitting (ρ',σ') of an extension of a Teichmüller-type group by a module lies in the units·module part, because the centre of the quotient is trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer of a section / automorphisms of extensions with centreless quotient
ideas.where_published: Related themes in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme; not this computation

ideas.what: Explicit cocycle-type linear equations (1−ρ)λ + 2νξ + νλ_1 = 0 and (1−σ)λ + 2νη = 0 for λu_μ to commute with the twisted generators, with u_μ acting by a cyclotomic-like exponent (ζ ↦ ζ^μ, ρ ↦ λ_1^ν ρ).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/cyclotomic-character action on the modular group and its abelianized extensions; nonabelian cocycle computation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld (GT), Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura for related explicit formulas

deep.surprise_reason: A routine explicit linear-algebra computation inside an ongoing study of splittings and lifts for the (genus 0 / modular) Teichmüller group. It is consistent with known themes later developed via GT and the cyclotomic character; nothing new is visible on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'dans G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G' (subscript μ_G rather than μ_ρ), also in (258).
'L'image de ce commutant dans (G_3)_{ρ_0} ≃ (G_{ρ,σ}/M)/O_12^* est contenue dans le centre de (G_3)_{ρ_0}, donc est triviale, d'où on conclut'.
(259) reads roughly 'Im_{G_{ρ,σ}/μ_G}(H(ρ',σ')) ⊂ O_12^*·M = G_{ρ,σ}^♮ ...' (with a crossed-out word), equal to {λu_μ | λ ∈ ΓM, μ ∈ ΓO_12^*}.
'On va donc déterminer ce centralisateur H(ρ',σ') en exprimant la condition pour un λu_μ d'y être' — not 'le centralisateur de H'.
In the displayed equations, the symbol written as ζ corresponds to ξ of the previous page.
